changes.newText: The Start From URL dialog has one tab per import source: Import Notebook, Import GitHub Repository, and Import GitLab Repository. An additional Import Hugging Face Model tab appears when the experimental Hugging Face import is turned on.

changes.newText: Import notebook
changes.newHtml: Import notebook

changes.newText: ./images/start_from_url_notebook.png
Enter a Jupyter Notebook URL (must end with .ipynb) in the Notebook URL field
changes.newHtml: Enter a Jupyter Notebook URL (must end with .ipynb) in the Notebook URL field

changes.newText: Click Import & Run to automatically create a session and open the notebook in Jupyter You can also click the dropdown arrow next to the button and select Start with options to customize the session environment before launching.
changes.newHtml:
Click Import & Run to automatically create a session and open the notebook in Jupyter

You can also click the dropdown arrow next to the button and select Start with options to customize the session environment before launching.

changes.newText: NOTE

The notebook is downloaded from inside the compute session (its bootstrap script runs curl -O <url>), so the URL must be reachable from the session. Local addresses such as localhost or 127.0.0.1 resolve to the session container itself — not your own machine — and will not work. Use a URL that is reachable from the compute session.
changes.newHtml: The notebook is downloaded from inside the compute session (its bootstrap script runs curl -O <url>), so the URL must be reachable from the session. Local addresses such as localhost or 127.0.0.1 resolve to the session container itself — not your own machine — and will not work. Use a URL that is reachable from the compute session.

changes.newText: NOTE
Turn off your browser's pop-up blocker so the running notebook window can open automatically. If there are not enough resources to start the session, the imported notebook will not run.

changes.newText: Import Hugging Face Model
changes.newHtml: Import Hugging Face Model

changes.newText: The Import Hugging Face Model tab downloads a model from Hugging Face into one of your model folders, so you can later mount it in a compute session or serve it as a deployment.
changes.newHtml: The Import Hugging Face Model tab downloads a model from Hugging Face into one of your model folders, so you can later mount it in a compute session or serve it as a deployment.

changes.newText: Experimental feature
This tab is hidden until you turn on Import from Hugging Face in the Experimental features section of the User Settings page. Experimental features may change or be removed in future updates.
changes.newHtml: This tab is hidden until you turn on Import from Hugging Face in the Experimental features section of the User Settings page. Experimental features may change or be removed in future updates.

changes.newText: ./images/start_from_url_huggingface.png

Enter the model in the Hugging Face Model URL or ID field. Both a model page URL such as https://huggingface.co/openai/gpt-oss-20b and a plain model ID such as openai/gpt-oss-20b are accepted. Addresses that point to a dataset, a space, or any other non-model page are rejected. Once the field contains a valid model, the dialog looks it up on Hugging Face after a short pause — a loading indicator shows while it checks — and displays a preview card below the field before you start the import. The card shows the model ID as a link to its Hugging Face page, the model's task and library tags, its size, and when it was last updated.
changes.newHtml:
Enter the model in the Hugging Face Model URL or ID field. Both a model page URL such as https://huggingface.co/openai/gpt-oss-20b and a plain model ID such as openai/gpt-oss-20b are accepted. Addresses that point to a dataset, a space, or any other non-model page are rejected.

Once the field contains a valid model, the dialog looks it up on Hugging Face after a short pause — a loading indicator shows while it checks — and displays a preview card below the field before you start the import. The card shows the model ID as a link to its Hugging Face page, the model's task and library tags, its size, and when it was last updated.

changes.newText: Optionally enter a Revision — the branch, tag, or commit of the model repository to download. Leave it empty to download the default revision. If the address you entered already contains a revision, that revision is used.
changes.newHtml: Optionally enter a Revision — the branch, tag, or commit of the model repository to download. Leave it empty to download the default revision. If the address you entered already contains a revision, that revision is used.

changes.newText: Optionally enter a Hugging Face Token. A token is required for gated or private models.
changes.newHtml: Optionally enter a Hugging Face Token. A token is required for gated or private models.

changes.newText: Select the Model Folder to download into. As the helper text under the field notes, only model folders in the current project that you can mount with write permission are listed — the download session writes into the folder, so folders you can only mount read-only are excluded. The buttons next to the selector let you open the selected folder, create a new model folder, and refresh the list.
changes.newHtml: Select the Model Folder to download into. As the helper text under the field notes, only model folders in the current project that you can mount with write permission are listed — the download session writes into the folder, so folders you can only mount read-only are excluded. The buttons next to the selector let you open the selected folder, create a new model folder, and refresh the list.

changes.newText: Click Download Model To Folder.
changes.newHtml: Click Download Model To Folder.

changes.newText: The dialog closes and Backend.AI starts a batch session that performs the download. Because the download runs inside that session, you can follow its progress on the Sessions page; the model is ready once the session finishes successfully. If the session fails, the download did not complete and the model is not ready to use.
changes.newHtml:
The dialog closes and Backend.AI starts a batch session that performs the
download. Because the download runs inside that session, you can follow its
progress on the Sessions page; the model is ready once the session finishes

changes.newText: The model is stored in a subfolder named after the model, inside the folder you selected — openai/gpt-oss-20b, for example, is downloaded to gpt-oss-20b/. Several models can therefore share a single model folder.
changes.newHtml: The model is stored in a subfolder named after the model, inside the folder you selected — openai/gpt-oss-20b, for example, is downloaded to gpt-oss-20b/. Several models can therefore share a single model folder.

changes.newText: WARNING
The token is passed to the download session as the HF_TOKEN environment variable and can be viewed by administrators. Use a read-only token.
changes.newHtml: The token is passed to the download session as the HF_TOKEN environment variable and can be viewed by administrators. Use a read-only token.

changes.newText: NOTE

The tab downloads into model folders, so it is only available when the deployment feature is enabled for your account. Large models take a long time to download and consume the storage quota of the target folder.
